content.text: “your boring life is beautiful”

“Picture yourself at the end of your life, on your deathbed. You’ve lived a good full life, but you can barely move or function anymore. Many of your loved ones have already passed on. But you get to go back to one day. You get to go back to this exact day that you’re in right now. You can’t change what you’re doing or anything. You just get to experience it one more time. Would you feel a little different about … that dull life you think you have?”
— Jake Frew

This thought comes from Jake Frew’s video “your boring life is beautiful.” In the video he shares about how frustrating and boring daily life can be, but then he shares this powerful thought about how with a different perspective — our own perspective but from the end of our life — we would view an otherwise dull or boring regular day as something beautiful and amazing. What do you think of this thought? Does it give you a different perspective on your life? Can you see your daily life from the perspective of yourself at the end of your life? How does that perspective change how you experience your everyday existence? Share the thoughts and feelings that come to mind as your consider this perspective.
Narrative option: tell the story of the day you get to relive, from the perspective of yourself at the end of your life.

content.text: Monster Support Group

Halloween is an exciting time for monsters. People love monsters during Halloween. And the best part for the monsters: they can actually go out and run around in the world and people just think they are wearing really impressive costumes. But, sadly, the rest of the year can be pretty hard for them. They have to keep hidden, and if they get spotted (in a closet or under a bed), it’s a stressful situation for them. But luckily these monsters have a support group: a time when they gather together and share their feelings and stories about how hard it is to be a monster in this world. You need to tell the story of this monster support group, or you can choose to tell one of the stories that a monster shares at this support group. Can you create unique and relatable monster characters with distinct personalities, backgrounds, and struggles? Can you share how these monsters feel about their lives and how they feel about humans and the hopes that they have for their futures?

content.text: “That’s how life is! We are all going to die before we put it all together.”
— Frank Bidart
This writing prompt has two options: explaining your thinking about the quote or creating a narrative related to the quote:

Explanatory option: Reflect on this idea from Frank Bidart. What do you think of it? Do you think you will be able to “put it all together”? What does that even mean? Could there be something reassuring or even beautiful in the acceptance that life is likely to be incomplete or imperfect? Does considering life’s incompleteness or imperfection change the way you think about or approach life? Share what comes to mind for you related to this quotation.

Narrative option: Imagine a character who has spent their whole life on a quest to figure out what matters most in life and to “put it all together.” Tell the story of their life as they approach the end of it without everything figured out and put all together.

content.text: A Mysterious, Ancient Egg

Recently, archaeologists discovered a fully intact egg that is at least 1,700 years old. The egg was found in England at an Iron-Age Roman site and is the oldest unintentionally preserved, unbroken egg in the world. And they still don’t know what it is or what’s in it ….
Pick the story you want to tell about the egg …
Scientists are able to extract the DNA from the egg and bring back something that has long been extinct …
The egg is put into an incubator, and it hatches something that was only thought to exist in myths and legends …
Scientists open the egg and unknowingly release … an ancient virus or ancient magic?
Or come up with your own story idea about the egg …

content.text: Never Meet Your Heroes

Have you heard that phrase, “never meet your heroes”? It’s fairly common advice, and it probably has something to do with the idea that the person that shows up in popular media is not the same as the real person, who is often disappointing in comparison. This probably happens because we tend to idealize our heroes in our minds, and the real person probably can’t live up to that ideal.

All that said, do you ever imagine what it would be like to meet one of your heroes? Who would you be interested in meeting and how do you imagine it going? What would you talk about? How would that conversation go? What do you think you would say or ask? What do you think they would share with you? Do you think the “never meet your heroes” advice would be true for them? In other words, do you think the idealized version of them might not match up to the real person? Share your thinking on meeting one of your heroes.

USA Today shared an article about how the World Happiness Report shows a significant decline in happiness of young Americans. The article speculates about the causes but notes that “researchers agree that there’s no one cause for the decline, rather a cluster of factors that’s driving young people to dissatisfaction….” What do you think of this? Does this decline in happiness make sense to you? Why do you think young people in the U.S. are reporting lower levels of happiness compared to previous generations and compared to young people in some other parts of the world? Do you have ideas for what could be done about this?
Share your thinking and make sure to use details and examples to support what you have to say.
